title: kate-text: return the scalar after an offset
summary: char_after returns the next scalar. The end of the buffer returns None. The body uses ?. The test goes in the existing buffer tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition: pub fn char_after(&self, at: Offset) -> Option<char>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: buffer.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Add char_after on impl TextBuffer. Keep it public, the same way char_before is public. Do not add a dead_code attribute. The body uses checked_add and ?. Then it calls char_at. Do not match on Some and None by hand. Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not write two if arms that return the same value. Combine them with ||. That is clippy::if_same_then_else. Do not touch char_at, char_before, or last_char. The existing test char_before_is_none_at_the_start stays green. Do not rewrite its assertions. The test char_after_is_none_at_the_end uses TextBuffer::from_str of ab. char_after of Offset(0) is Some of b. char_after of Offset(1) is None. char_after of Offset(2) is None. An empty buffer at Offset(0) is None. A buffer of one e-acute at Offset(0) is None. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Stay inside this one behavior. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: buffer::tests::char_after_is_none_at_the_end
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because char_after does not exist. After the change offset 0 of ab is b. The last scalar and an empty buffer return None.
